title: Tail-read backstop spacing resets on reads that carry no new demand, so busy workspaces stay near 3 s
outcome: The backstop's per-session spacing resets only when that session's tail demand actually changes. An unrelated state event or a watchdog re-read leaves an uncertified session's backoff in place.
acceptance: The spacing resets on a real change in that session's demand, for example a per-session demand generation that advances when its observed body sequence moves or a certified tail becomes dirty. It no longer resets on every non-backstop read or request, such as the startVisibleTranscriptRepairs and adoptSessions sweeps or the 15 s watchdog's reads.
A Vitest test shows that a state event leaving this session's bodySeq unchanged keeps its backed-off spacing, and that the existing reset tests still pass.
The change lands under the standing rule.
